clue.text: Almost change direction when this old learner's sat inside it?

definitions.text: Almost change direction when this old learner's sat inside it?

indicators.note: sat inside says the other pieces are placed within the shortened word
almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to veer is to change direction
hic is Latin, an old language, for 'this'
L is the learner's plate abbreviation

explanation.surface: A driver nearly swerves as an elderly learner takes the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: Latin counts as the 'old' language here, so 'this old' gives its word for 'this'. Read whole, the clue also pictures a car with a learner at the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is a conveyance in which a learner driver sits, so the whole clue paints one.

clue.text: Lady holding on to find from where gentlemen came?

indicators.note: holding means the lady's name wraps around the other word

parts.note: Vera is a woman's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman clutches something to discover the origin of some gents.
explanation.walkthrough: Refers to Shakespeare's The Two Gentlemen of Verona.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's two gentlemen came from this Italian city, as the play's title says.

clue.text: What real-ale manufacturer does by the book?

definitions.meaning: a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: A craft brewer works strictly by the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as HE BREWS for the first sense; the second is a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epistle to the Hebrews is a New Testament book, and a brewer is someone who brews.

clue.text: Select via corruption —- it's just as you'd expect!

indicators.note: corruption signals the letters are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: Choose bribery: that's how things go!
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means 'that's life', a shrug at what was always going to happen.

clue.text: Times in link up leading to demise

indicators.note: in says the sign is placed inside the turned word
up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tie is a link
X is the multiplication sign, times

explanation.surface: Times newspaper ties leading to someone's death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TIE to EIT; 'in' puts X inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit, a departure from the stage, is a euphemism for death.

clue.text: Left one wearing an outfit that's filthy

indicators.note: wearing means the outfit goes around the other letters like clothing

parts.note: a squad is a team or outfit
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone left alone in a uniform that is grubby.
explanation.definitionFit: Squalid is a synonym for dirty and wretched.

clue.text: Fight over several tips

parts.note: a scrap is a fight
heaps means lots of

explanation.surface: A punch-up over a handful of gratuities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips' are rubbish dumps in British English, not gratuities.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapheaps are rubbish piles, which British speakers call tips.

clue.text: Early developments in these partially computerised

indicators.note: partially means only part of the word is used, the run inside it

explanation.surface: Early stages of growth here are partly done by computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wombs are where embryos make their first growth before birth.

clue.text: Radical allowed to intermingle a little with duke

indicators.note: intermingle a little says the two words mix slightly, a small reordering of their letters

parts.note: let means allowed
dukes is slang for fists

explanation.surface: An extremist was permitted to mix a bit with an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duke' is slang for a fist ('put up your dukes'); LET and FIST mixed give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical in politics is an extremist of the left.

clue.text: Meditate on this: I retired from fives, from point of view of being sixty

definitions.text: fives, from point of view of being sixty

parts.note: to do Zen is to meditate

indicators.note: retired from means the letter leaves the word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thoughtful instruction, then a man quits a game of fives at sixty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired from' takes I out of THIS. Five is a twelfth of sixty, so each five is one of twelve parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Five is one twelfth of sixty, so relative to sixty each five is a twelfth part.

clue.text: Revolutionary opponents set Englishman and Frenchman apart

parts.note: Rob is a typical English man's name
E and S, East and South, are opponents at bridge
Pierre is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: Rivals divide an English and a French man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set ... apart' just says the opponents stand between the two men; at bridge East and South sit on opposing sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Robespierre was a leading figure of the French Revolution.

clue.text: Cover for nut made. of iron plus something unknown

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A protective cap for a bolt's nut is made of iron and a mystery metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nut' is slang for the head, so its cover is a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Nut is slang for head, and a fez is a hat worn on it.

clue.text: Sulphur compound's regular pattern found in nickel alloys

indicators.note: a regular pattern found in the words means keep two letters, drop two, and repeat through them

explanation.surface: A sulphur compound forms an ordered structure inside nickel alloys.
explanation.walkthrough: From NICKELALLOYS keep NI, drop CK, keep EL, drop AL, keep LO, drop YS: a regular two-on, two-off pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Niello is a black mixture of sulphur with silver, copper or lead used to fill engraving.

clue.text: One accepts being confused by his small print

definitions.text: One accepts being confused by his small print

indicators.note: accepts means the jumbled word takes the other letter inside it
being confused says the letters of the small print are jumbled

parts.note: a caption is the small print under a picture
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An eye specialist puts up with patients being baffled by his tiny test letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being confused' scrambles CAPTION to OPTICAN, which 'accepts' I. The whole clue also describes the eye tester.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye tester shows patients a chart of tiny letters, which may well confuse them.

clue.text: Rest in snooker, for example

parts.note: taken as written
snooker is an example of a pastime or activity

explanation.surface: Using the cue support called the rest at snooker.
explanation.walkthrough: A rest is also a cue support in snooker, which misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Inactivity means idleness, the state of resting.

clue.text: Y-Y-Y-Y-Y-Y-Yen for getting flat with old baggage?

parts.words: Y-Y-Y-Y-Y-Y-Yen for getting flat with old baggage?
parts.note: seven letter Ys stand for seven years (Y is short for year), and yen means an itch or longing

explanation.surface: A stammering confession of longing to move out from an ageing partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Count the Ys: seven, each Y standing for year; 'Yen' is a craving, an itch. The rest pictures a spouse wanting to leave the 'old baggage' (wife) for a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the supposed urge to stray after some years of marriage, here leaving the old partner.

clue.text: According to report, lounge, say, and loft are possibly suffering from damp

indicators.note: according to report signals that the words are as heard spoken

parts.note: a lounge is an example of a room, and a loft is an attic

explanation.surface: Damp houses are said to be blighted in every room.
explanation.walkthrough: ROOM + ATTIC spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheumatic pains are traditionally blamed on damp weather or houses.

clue.text: Bird high on bill seen to change sides at one point

indicators.text: to change sides at one point
indicators.note: change sides at one point means one R (right) becomes L (left)

parts.note: a star at the top of the billing is seen starring

explanation.surface: A bird perched on a beak switches sides.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap one R for L in the word meaning top-billed.
explanation.definitionFit: The starling is a common songbird.

clue.text: Some change gift for Peter into what may suit

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a two-piece is a suit of jacket and trousers
Peter's pence was the annual payment to the Pope, St Peter's successor

explanation.surface: Small change as a present for Peter, converted into something fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: The two-pence piece is a British coin, so it is 'some change'.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-pence piece is a coin, part of the loose change in a pocket.

clue.text: Melodious harp one played

indicators.note: played suggests the words are performed in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A tuneful harp played solo.
explanation.definitionFit: Orphean means melodious, like the music of Orpheus.

clue.text: Capture enemies near their headquarters, resisting allied landings on the front

indicators.note: on the front points at the leading letter of each word

parts.words: enemies near their headquarters, resisting allied landings

explanation.surface: A war order to seize enemy bases while fighting off Allied landings.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthral is to captivate, capturing someone's attention.

clue.text: Legal English is above being exact

indicators.note: is above in a down clue puts the letter on top of the word

parts.note: licit means legal

explanation.surface: Lawful English trumps precision.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact a response is to draw it out, which is to elicit it.

clue.text: One's expected to talk over scores in it

definitions.text: One's expected to talk over scores in it

parts.words: One's expected to talk over scores in it
parts.note: a performer of this style speaks rhythmically over backing tracks rather than singing the score

explanation.surface: In this genre a performer must speak over the music.
explanation.definitionFit: Rappers chant words over a musical backing instead of singing, which is the genre's defining feature.

clue.text: Spotted article dropped off for relative

indicators.note: dropped off means the letters fall away from the word

parts.note: spotted can mean soiled or unclean
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A stained newspaper piece is delivered to a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: Your parent's brother is a family member, a relative.

clue.text: A mum needs to pound a large banger?

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mum
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A mother has to bash a big sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banger' looks like a British sausage but means an explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: Amatol is a high explosive, a big banger in the firework sense.

clue.text: Stuff found on black post

parts.note: to jam is to stuff
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: Preserve found on a dark pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is the upright post at the side of a door or window.

clue.text: Individualise symmetrically filleted fish

indicators.note: filleted symmetrically means equal stretches are cut from each side of the middle, leaving first, central and last letters

explanation.surface: Treat each filleted fish in a balanced way.
explanation.walkthrough: INDIVIDUALISE has thirteen letters; take out five each side of the central D, leaving I, D and E.
explanation.definitionFit: The ide is a freshwater fish, also called the orfe.

clue.text: Critical period in terrible Arctic clime

indicators.note: terrible signals that the words are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A crucial time to be stuck in dreadful polar weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A climacteric is a critical stage or turning point, as in life.

clue.text: Sort of firing head of convent having found replacement

indicators.note: head of points at the opening letter of the word
having found replacement means that opening letter is swapped for another

parts.note: a nunnery is a convent

explanation.surface: A mother superior has been replaced at the convent.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the N at the head of NUNNERY to G; the clue does not say where G comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunnery is the firing of large guns, so it is a sort of shooting.

clue.text: Champion's destiny in a major set

parts.note: to champion a cause is to back it
one's lot is one's fate

explanation.surface: A winner's fate in a major tennis set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'major set' hints at film studios, not tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlot is a large outdoor area at a film studio where sets are built.
